subject: Request: one-time sandbox runway + allocation exception for Summit Healthworks POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Morris <evan.morris@summithealthworks.com>, Nora Patel <nora@helden.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: one-time sandbox runway + allocation exception for Summit Healthworks POC

Team —

Quick context: Summit Healthworks is running a 30-day sandbox POC (deal DL-2026-097). Procurement just informed the buyer that their security review will push the start of customer-side testing out by ~6 weeks. If we do not extend their sandbox and give them additional consumable allocation, the POC will expire before they can finish integration and evaluation.

What I'm asking for:
- One-time extension of the sandbox window from 30 -> 120 days (start date remains unchanged).
- One-time increase in consumable allocation to 250k tokens (standard PLG cap is 50k tokens).

Why this matters:
- Summit is a top-10 target in healthcare vertical; expected ARR if they move forward is ~$1.2M in year 1.
- The technical blocker is the SOC2 evidence and SSO configuration scheduled for Aug 18; until then they cannot run integration tests at scale.
- They are not asking for a discount; this is purely runway and usage to prove the integration.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (MVP acceptance criteria + timeline), Security_Summary_Extract.txt (customer-specific controls asked for).

Risks / guardrails proposed:
- Limit this to a single, one-time exception for Summit D L-2026-097.
- AUTO-terminate sandbox if not active for 14 consecutive days after extended start of tests.
- No automatic billing changes; if they convert, normal pricing applies.

Ask: Marissa — can you approve as a one-off deal-desk escalation? Karthik — anything from compliance or ops I should note? Laura — if this needs SVP signoff, please advise.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (1.1MB)
Attachment: Security_Summary_Extract.txt (12KB)

Jonas — thanks for the clear ask and the MA P. Quick clarifying q's before I escalate formally:
1) Can you confirm the POC success criteria and what measurable signal will trigger an internal conversion discussion? (e.g., throughput tests + 3 reference prompts scoring >= 0.8 on their eval harness)
2) Is legal expecting any contract addendum for extended usage? If yes, please attach the proposed addendum text.

I think this is reasonable given the account potential, but I want to be explicit about the guardrails so we don't set a precedent. If we escalate, I will ask SVP revenue for a one-time exception authority.

Pls loop in legal/finance if any downstream changes to invoicing or data residency are required.

—Marissa

Thanks for moving quickly. To confirm from our side:
- Procurement pushed our internal start date to Sep 1 due to an unexpected legal review.
- We need the ability to run end-to-end integration tests at scale (500+ calls/day) to validate SLAs and error handling.

Marissa / Jonas —

From an ops/compliance perspective: we can support the sandbox extension and one-time allocation increase with the following constraints:
- Maximum allowed exception without CFO signoff: extend to 90 days and allocation <= 150k tokens.
- Any allocation >150k tokens or extension >90 days requires finance approval (possible revenue recognition / usage exposure).
- We should add a written MA P milestone that triggers deactivation if idle for 14 days.

If legal signs off on a one-off addendum that limits financial exposure and affirms no automatic billing changes, I'm happy to route the final ask to Finance for approval of the larger uplift.

Karthik
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the notes and the diligence. After reviewing the MA P and expected ARR, I'm comfortable approving a limited exception with explicit guardrails. Approvals granted: 

- Sandbox extension granted: 30 -> 120 days (one-time exception)
- Consumable allocation granted: 200,000 tokens (one-time exception)

Conditions:
1) This is explicitly a single, non-precedent-setting exception tied to deal DL-2026-097 (Summit Healthworks).
2) Legal must sign a short addendum confirming the extension and allocation cap; no billing changes without a conversion order.
3) Sales Ops to configure auto-deactivate if sandbox idle >14 days and to tag the account as "escalation-exception:DL-2026-097".
4) If usage appears to be abusive or outside of the MA P, Redwood may revoke the privilege immediately.

Marissa — please document this approval in the deal record and notify Finance & Legal to prepare the addendum and enable the sandbox config. Jonas — please get Evan to confirm the acceptance criteria in writing (email is fine) so we have a clear conversion trigger.

Laura Bennett
SVP, Revenue | Redwood Inference
